name: NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack (72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs): fully liquid-cooled, Max TDP up to 1,400 W per GPU
notes: The high-water mark for a single accelerator's power envelope in any shipping NVIDIA rack. Technical Specifications table: GB300 NVL72 per-Blackwell-Ultra-GPU Max TDP is 'Configurable up to 1,400 W'; the 8-GPU HGX B300 sibling is 'Configurable up to 1,100 W'. The generation ladder from datasheets in this repo: H100 SXM 700 W, H100 PCIe 350 W, HGX B200 up to 1,000 W, HGX B300 up to 1,100 W, GB200 NVL72/NVL4 up to 1,200 W, GB300 NVL72 up to 1,400 W - roughly 2x Hopper per GPU in two generations, with a notably non-monotonic ordering between B200 (1000 W) and GB200 NVL72 (1200 W) that reflects rack context rather than silicon. COOLING IS EXPLICIT AND TOTAL: 'The NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 features a fully liquid-cooled, rack-scale architecture that integrates 72 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Arm-based NVIDIA Grace CPUs into a single platform'. This is the generation where liquid stops being partial (GB200 liquid-cooled CPUs and GPUs via cold plates but air-cooled networking and storage) and becomes the rack's defining characteristic. THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER ON THIS PAGE IS NOT THE WATTAGE - IT IS THE DENOMINATOR. NVIDIA's own performance charts for both GB300 NVL72 and HGX B300 normalize throughput to 'Tokens per Second (TPS) in 1 MW (Throughput)' - the vendor is now selling tokens per megawatt of facility power rather than tokens per GPU. That is the clearest possible vendor admission that at this density power is the binding unit of account and compute is not. Practical consequence: a 1,400 W per-GPU ceiling with 72 GPUs implies a rack envelope in the same neighbourhood as GB200 NVL72 (the exact GB300 rack power figure is NOT published in the datasheet - do not infer one), so a facility that cannot take GB200 cannot take GB300 either. Rack power for GB300 is recorded as unknown rather than extrapolated.
